research_question: How much resident-state tax is created when parallel workers privately replicate the same immutable capability, and how much of that tax can verified shared immutable backing remove?

hosted_proxy.metric: sum of worker PSS from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup with same-worker-count baseline subtraction
hosted_proxy.semantic_gate: SHA256 equality for PRIVATE_COPY and SHARED_MMAP

primary_oracles: all capability digests match the frozen source payload
one-worker private and shared capability growth are both positive after baseline subtraction
PRIVATE_COPY normalized PSS growth from one to four workers scales by at least 2.5x
SHARED_MMAP normalized PSS growth from one to four workers scales by at most 2.0x
four-worker SHARED_MMAP normalized growth is at most 60% of PRIVATE_COPY normalized growth
nonclaims: Lower PSS is not a throughput improvement claim.
The experiment does not select a universal worker count.
Shared mmap is not assumed to remove page-fault, cache, contention, or coordination costs.
GitHub-hosted Linux PSS behavior is not a universal RAM law.
Shared availability does not grant execution authority.
net_parallel_gain_candidate: QueueReduction + UsefulConcurrency - ResidencyTax - Contention - Coordination - VerificationOverhead
next_falsifier: Add queueing/useful-progress and contention measurements across worker counts so residency savings cannot be mistaken for net parallel speedup.
